exhibits.title: The Whisper Beside the Weight
exhibits.text:
A slender branch of light stands BESIDE the frozen tapestry, not after it. When the same input x arrives, it strikes both at once: the great frozen W does its full work, and this thin taper does a small work of its own, and their lights are ADDED where they meet. The taper is the LoRA branch, and it whispers a correction rather than replacing a word.

A great confusion to burn away here: LoRA is NOT a layer bolted on at the END of W, taking W's output and transforming it further. It is a SIDE BRANCH, running in PARALLEL, fed the very same input x that W is fed. Sequentially stacking would mean 'reshape what W already said'; running in parallel means 'ADD a small learned delta to what W already does'. LoRA wants the second. So the full computation of the adapted layer is

    y  =  W . x  +  B . A . x

One input x, two paths, one summed output y. Freeze the tapestry; let the taper beside it whisper how much to adjust. The artifact enacts it: motes of signal stream from the d inputs on the left, CONVERGE through a narrow waist of just r nodes, the bottleneck that forces the correction to be low-rank, then fan back out to d on the right, all beside the dim, frozen slab of W they are added to.

exhibits.title: A Parallel Branch, Not a Later Layer
exhibits.text:
A plain linear layer computes y = W . x. The instinct on first hearing 'add A and B' is to imagine them appended AFTER W, so the signal passes through W and then through A and B in sequence. That is the wrong picture, and it is worth correcting precisely.

LoRA keeps W exactly as it is and adds a second path that sees the SAME input x. The two paths run side by side and their outputs are SUMMED:

    y  =  W . x  +  B . A . x

Read the two terms plainly. W . x is what the frozen, pretrained layer already does, untouched. B . A . x is the learned correction, the 'delta', computed from the identical x and added on top. Because they share the input and add their outputs, the branch cannot distort W's answer; it can only nudge it. That is exactly what fine-tuning wants: not to re-transform the base model's output, but to add a small, learned adjustment beside it.

exhibits.title: The Bottleneck That Forces Low Rank
exhibits.text:
Follow the input along the whisper-branch and watch its width change. The input x is a vector of length d. First A acts:

    x      : (d,)     the full-width input
    A . x  : (r,)     A is r x d, so it SQUEEZES x down to just r numbers
    B (A.x): (d,)     B is d x r, so it EXPANDS back up to d

The middle line is the whole trick. Everything the branch will contribute must pass through a channel only r numbers wide, the BOTTLENECK. With r = 8, no matter how large d is, the branch's entire message is throttled to 8 numbers before it is re-expanded. A composition that squeezes to r and expands from r can produce a d x d effect of rank AT MOST r; it is structurally incapable of a full-rank update. So the low rank is not asked for politely and hoped for. It is FORCED by the shape of the path. The bottleneck is the mechanism; low rank is its guarantee. Widen r and you widen the channel, letting a richer correction through at the price of more parameters, the trade weighed in the chambers ahead.

exhibits.title: One Input, Two Paths, One Sum
exhibits.spec:
graph LR
  X["x  (d,)"] --> W["W . x  (frozen)"]
  X --> A["A  r x d"]
  A --> AX["A . x  (r,)  BOTTLENECK"]
  AX --> B["B  d x r"]
  B --> BAX["B . A . x  (d,)"]
  W --> SUM(("+"))
  BAX --> SUM
  SUM --> Y["y = W.x + B.A.x  (d,)"]
exhibits.caption: The same input x fans into two parallel paths: the frozen W . x, and the LoRA branch A then B. Along the branch the width squeezes to the rank-r bottleneck (A . x is only r numbers) and expands back to d (B . A . x). The two outputs are summed to y. The r-wide waist is what forces the correction to be low-rank.

exhibits.title: The Whisper, Traced Beside the Weight
exhibits.caption: Trace the whisper beside the weight. (a) One input x arrives and fans into TWO parallel paths, never in sequence: above, the frozen W does its full work to give W . x; below, the LoRA branch feeds the SAME x through A, down to the narrow waist A . x, then out through B to B . A . x. The two outputs meet at the sum, y = W . x + B . A . x. Each node is drawn to its dimension, wide where the signal is d numbers across, pinched narrow where it is only r. (b) The shape trace makes the pinch exact: x carries d = 1000 numbers, A . x squeezes to just r = 8, and B . A . x expands back to d = 1000. Everything the branch can contribute must pass through that r-wide throat, so the correction it adds can have rank at most r. The bottleneck is the mechanism; low rank is its guarantee.
